questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
For me the courses I could choose at the University was important but what made New Zealand 
really special to me was the stunning nature and the laid back, friendly culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: VUW was a really great place to be an international stuedent and you got a great welcome with lots of information and social events.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Help with accommodation, finances, studies, social events, ect. They were super helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: They had several types of housing, both catered and non-catered places depending on preference. Some were small shared houses and others were apartents - both shared and individual. You had an option to make a top 3 choices. Most housing was centered around the university but few were also downtown or further away.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Catered or not

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I would recommend campus housing, but do not have too high expectations - especially when coming from Denmark. Most housing in NZ, both on and off campus, is rather run down and not in great condition. Also, no one has central heating, so expect houses to be cold, although most have electric heaters in the rooms. I thought it was fine for 4-5 months of living and I was quite happy with my room/house in general.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You applied for a spot, got accepted and then choose courses. They have the portals: Puaha and Nuku which are their uni-sites for students where all you information and courses are.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They had a whole site for internationals and a support e-mail where they responded quickly - very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very. I even chose different ones after I arrived.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just ask a lot of questions if in doubt and they will help you out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had 3 BA: I had one first year course, very easy, one second year course, very easy and one third year course which was a field trip - quite intense but amazing and easy to get through.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Only 50min lectures at a time and som courses have lab/pratical hours as well but it varies quite a lot.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Antarctica: Unfreezing the continent
Volcanic Field Geology
Earth Materials and Resources
Environmental Futures for Aotearoa New Zealand

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Antartica can be enjoyed by everyone: super interesting and very easy

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: So many different types of clubs were at VUW. Language, music, sports, games etc. I think everyone could find something interesting.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did fencing and kayaking which was super fun.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go hiking and explore!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. Very friendly community.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It is a lot of work. If you want local friends you have to put in an effort and show them consistently. You can tell that they have a lot of internationals so its up to you to make them notice you.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The outdoors mindset. Love being outside and doing activities together that is based in nature.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Put on a smile, keep and open mind, and enjoy ;) 
Do not have huge expectations for everything to work out the way you wanted it to or for every day to be amazing but take it as it comes and just experience it.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends I made along the way.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Prioritizing uni when there are so many fun things to do.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
